topic: First farm day, told to Yuki
title_jp: {一日目|いちにちめ}の{気持|きも}ち
context: Your first full day on the Tanaka farm started at 5 a.m. Tonight Yuki, your friend in Tokyo, messages you on LINE to ask how it went. Today: describing how you feel and what people around you are like.

phrases.jp: {慣れない|なれない|to get used to|3}{生活|せいかつ|daily life|3}で、ちょっと{疲|つか}れ{気味|ぎみ|a bit, slightly (so)|2}です。
phrases.en: This new life I'm not used to has left me a bit tired.
phrases.note: 〜{気味|ぎみ} = a touch of: {疲|つか}れ{気味|ぎみ}, {風邪|かぜ}{気味|ぎみ} (a bit of a cold). Softer than just {疲|つか}れました.

phrases.jp: {家族|かぞく}のことを{思い出して|おもいだして|to remember, recall|3}、{寂しく|さびしく|lonely|3}なった。
phrases.en: I thought of my family and got lonely.
phrases.note: 〜くなる = became: {寂|さび}しくなった describes a feeling that came over you, not a permanent state.

phrases.jp: {緊張|きんちょう|nervousness, tension|3}して、{何|なに}も{言|い}えなかった。
phrases.en: I was so nervous I couldn't say anything.
phrases.note: {緊張|きんちょう}する is the everyday word for nervous (before a meeting, a test, a first date). Not {心配|しんぱい|worry|4}, which is worry.

phrases.jp: {田中|たなか}さんは{無口|むくち|quiet, of few words|2}だけど、{温|あたた}かい{人|ひと}です。
phrases.en: Tanaka-san doesn't say much, but he's a warm person.
phrases.note: Describing someone: [trait]だけど[trait]. {無口|むくち} is neutral, not rude: just a person of few words.

phrases.jp: {親|おや}を{心配|しんぱい|worry|4}させたくないから、{毎週|まいしゅう}{電話|でんわ}してる。
phrases.en: I don't want to make my parents worry, so I call every week.
phrases.note: {心配|しんぱい|worry|4}させる = make someone worry (causative). Very common with family: {親|おや}を{心配|しんぱい|worry|4}させないで！

dialogue_setting: A LINE chat at night: you're under the kotatsu in your upstairs room, Yuki is on the train home in Tokyo.

dialogue.speaker: 由紀
dialogue.jp: アル〜！{農家|のうか|farm, farming family|2}{生活|せいかつ|daily life|3}{一日目|いちにちめ}、どうだった？？
dialogue.en: Al~! Day one of farm life, how was it??

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: {疲|つか}れた〜ｗ 5{時|じ}に{起|お}きて、{一日中|いちにちじゅう|all day long|3}りんご{畑|ばたけ|field (farm)|2}にいた。でも{景色|けしき|view, scenery|3}がめっちゃきれい。{山|やま}が{真っ赤|まっか|bright red|3}だよ
dialogue.en: So tired lol. Up at 5, in the apple orchard all day. But the view is amazing. The mountains are bright red.

dialogue.speaker: 由紀
dialogue.jp: いいじゃん！で、{田中|たなか}さんってどんな{人|ひと}？{怖|こわ}い？
dialogue.en: Nice! So what's Tanaka-san like? Scary?

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: {無口|むくち|quiet, of few words|2}だけど{優|やさ}しいよ。{今日|きょう}、{畑|はたけ|field (farm)|2}で{軽|けい|軽トラ = mini truck|2}トラを{運転|うんてん|driving|3}させてくれた！
dialogue.en: He doesn't talk much but he's kind. Today he let me drive the kei truck in the field!

dialogue.speaker: 由紀
dialogue.jp: マジ！？いい{人|ひと}じゃん。でも{夜|よる}とか{寂しくない|さびしくない|lonely|3}？
dialogue.en: Seriously!? He sounds great. But don't you get lonely, like at night?

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: ちょっとね。{静|しず}かすぎて、スペインの{家族|かぞく}を{思い出す|おもいだす|to remember, recall|3}。まだ{慣れない|なれない|to get used to|3}けど、がんばる
dialogue.en: A little. It's so quiet I keep thinking of my family in Spain. Not used to it yet, but I'll hang in there.

dialogue.speaker: 由紀
dialogue.jp: えらい！{家族|かぞく}を{心配|しんぱい|worry|4}させないように、{写真|しゃしん}{送|おく}ってあげなよ
dialogue.en: Good on you! Send them some photos so they don't worry

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: うん、{明日|あした}{送|おく}る！{おやすみ||good night|4}
dialogue.en: Yeah, I'll send them tomorrow! Night

grammar.form: う-verbs: -a + せる ({行|い}く → {行|い}かせる) · る-verbs: + させる ({食|た}べる → {食|た}べさせる) · する → させる ({運転|うんてん}させる) · {来|く}る → {来|こ}させる
grammar.explanation: The causer is the subject and the person made or allowed to act gets に (or を with intransitive verbs): {親|おや}を{心配|しんぱい|worry|4}させる. Alone it often sounds like forcing; add てくれる / てもらう and it becomes kind permission: {運転|うんてん|driving|3}させてくれた = he let me drive. Don't mix it up with the passive (〜られる, something done to you) or the causative-passive (〜させられる, being made to do it).

examples.jp: {母|はは}は{毎日|まいにち}{私|わたし}に{野菜|やさい}を{食|た}べさせた。
examples.en: My mum made me eat vegetables every day.

examples.jp: {少|すこ}し{考|かんが}えさせてください。
examples.en: Please let me think about it a little.

examples.jp: {冗談|じょうだん|joke|3}を{言|い}って、みんなを{笑|わら}わせた。
examples.en: I told a joke and made everyone laugh.

quiz.question: {先生|せんせい}は{学生|がくせい}に{本|ほん}を＿＿。
quiz.en: The teacher made the students read the book.
quiz.explain: {読|よ}む → {読|よ}ませる: the teacher (subject) makes the students (に) read. {読|よ}まれた is passive, {読|よ}ませられた is being made to read, {読|よ}めた is could read.

quiz_more.question: {部長|ぶちょう|department head|3}は{新人|しんじん|new employee|3}にコピーを＿＿。
quiz_more.en: The manager made the new employee do the copying.
quiz_more.explain: Making someone do something: する → させる, and the person made to do it takes に.

quiz_more.question: {子|こ}どもたちを{公園|こうえん}で{自由|じゆう|freely|3}に＿＿。
quiz_more.en: I let the kids play freely in the park.
quiz_more.explain: う-verb: 遊ぶ → 遊ばせる. When it's something they want to do, the causative means 'let them'.

kanji.where: Under every message you send on LINE, the small grey 既読 appears as soon as the other person opens it.
kanji.related: 既読スルー (or 既読無視) = reading a message and not replying, a classic source of LINE drama.
kanji.breakdown: {既読|きどく}: 既 already + 読 read → 'already read'. LINE shows it under your message once the other person opens it.

tip.title: There's no one word for 'homesick'
tip.body: Japanese mostly borrows ホームシック: ホームシックになった. Among friends you can say {寂|さび}しい freely, but with your host family it can sound like you're unhappy with them and make them worry. Gentler: {家族|かぞく}にちょっと{会|あ}いたくなりました, or simply スペインが{恋しい|こいしい|恋しい = to miss (someone)|2}です (I miss Spain).

challenge.prompt: Yuki replies: 「{明日|あした}も5{時|じ}{起|お}き？{今|いま}の{気持|きも}ち、{一言|ひとこと|in a word|2}で！」 Tell her how you feel and one thing the Tanakas let you do, with 〜させてくれた.
challenge.hint: {眠|ねむ}い · {楽|たの}しい · {仕事|しごと}をやらせてくれた
challenge.model_answer: ちょっと{眠|ねむ}いけど、{楽|たの}しい！ケイコさんが{台所|だいどころ|kitchen|3}で{料理|りょうり}を{手伝わせて|てつだわせて|to help|3}くれたよ。
challenge.explanation: ちょっと{眠|ねむ}いけど、{楽|たの}しい！ answers 'in a word' with a contrast (けど = but). {手伝|てつだ}わせてくれた = {手伝|てつだ}う → causative {手伝|てつだ}わせる (let me help) + てくれた (as a kindness to me): 'Keiko let me help with the cooking.' The final よ is friendly LINE tone.

vocab.note: 〜に{慣|な}れる: {日本|にほん}の{生活|せいかつ}に{慣|な}れた？ is a question you'll hear a lot.

vocab.en: a touch of, slightly (after a noun or stem)

extras.title: Feelings, from mild to strong
extras.intro: Words for how you feel in a new place, the ones friends actually use.

items.en: my heart is pounding (excited or nervous)
to be excited, looking forward to it

items.jp: {落ち込む|おちこむ|to feel down|3}
items.note: {落|お}ち{込|こ}んでる？ = are you feeling down?
A happy feeling about the past, not sadness.

extras.title: Describing people
extras.intro: Answers to Yuki's question, for when someone asks about your host, coworker or a date.

items.jp: {明|あか}るくて{話|はな}しやすい。
items.en: Cheerful and easy to talk to.

items.jp: {真面目|まじめ|serious, earnest|3}な{人|ひと}。
ちょっと{人見知り|ひとみしり|shy with strangers|3}。
items.en: A bit shy with new people.
items.note: Very common self-description; no single English word.

items.jp: {面倒見|めんどうみ|caring for others|2}がいい。
